field.label: Enable
field.help: Watch the network for new devices.

field.label: Interfaces
field.help: Interfaces to watch. Leave empty to watch every interface. Excluding WAN is usually a good idea, as your provider's equipment would be reported too.

field.label: Scan interval
field.help: Seconds between two inspections of the ARP and NDP tables.

field.label: Include IPv6 neighbours
field.help: Also inspect the IPv6 neighbour (NDP) table, so IPv6-only devices are detected as well.

field.label: Learn silently on first run
field.help: When the device database is empty, record the devices found by the first scan without sending notifications. This avoids a flood of alerts for the devices already on your network.

field.label: New device
field.help: A MAC address that has never been seen before appeared on the network.

field.label: IP address changed MAC
field.help: An IP address is now used by a different MAC address than before. This can indicate ARP spoofing, but also happens when a DHCP lease is handed to another device. Reported at most once per hour per address.

field.label: Known device, new IP address
field.help: A known MAC address started using an IP address it did not use before. Noisy on networks using DHCP or IPv6 privacy addresses.

field.label: Ignore MAC addresses
field.help: MAC addresses or prefixes (e.g. 00:11:22) that never trigger a notification. They are still recorded in the device list.
